name: RNA (ribonucleic acid)
short_description: The working copy — usually single-stranded, folding back on itself into hairpins and stem-loops rather than pairing with a second strand along its whole length. Ribose stands in for deoxyribose (an extra -OH on the 2' carbon), and uracil stands in for thymine. Three working forms do the job: mRNA carries a gene's transcript from the nucleus to the ribosome, tRNA folds into an unmistakable cloverleaf/L-shape to ferry the matching amino acid, and rRNA folds into the bulk of the ribosome itself.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; mRNA correctly single-stranded, but baked-in text 'TN' appeared directly in the pixels next to the ribosome groove — a hard no-baked-text violation — and the tRNA read as a decorative bow/infinity-twist ribbon rather than a recognisable cloverleaf. Fix-prompt: forbid any letters/abbreviations near the ribosome, and redescribe the tRNA explicitly as a flat four-petal clover, not a woven ribbon)
textbook.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; no baked text this time, but the tRNA was still an ambiguous woven bow shape not clearly touching the mRNA codon, and — the more serious issue — the ribosome's subunit groove showed a vertical rung/ladder pattern that risked reading as a miniature DNA-style double helix. Two hard fails on this style — escalated to gemini-3-pro-image per the model ladder. Fix-prompt: explicit four-petal-clover geometry with a central hub and radiating spoke-stems, and an explicit ban on any rung/ladder motif outside the mRNA's own hairpin and the tRNA's own arms)
textbook.3: fail (gemini-3-pro-image; the escalation fixed the clover shape beautifully — a genuine, unambiguous four-petal cloverleaf with a clear separate amino-acid tail — and the ribosome/hairpin geometry was correct, but the model baked literal 'A'/'U'/'G'/'C' letter glyphs directly onto every coloured base bead along the mRNA strand, a hard violation despite explicit instructions. Fix-prompt: replace circular beads (which invite letter-writing) with plain non-circular tick-dashes, and add an explicit 'do not write single-character base letters even though it feels natural' instruction)
textbook.4: fail (gemini-3-pro-image; still baked full base-letter sequences onto every base marker despite the anti-glyph instruction and despite switching wording — the circular-bead motif reliably triggers this model's tendency to label nucleotides. Fix-prompt: eliminate all circular/oval marker shapes from the prompt entirely, since every failure so far involved a round marker being filled with text)
textbook.5: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; switching every base marker from a circular bead to a plain flat-colour tick-dash (no closed round shape anywhere on the mRNA) finally broke the letter-writing tendency — confirmed clean on a magnified crop with zero text anywhere. Final composition: a single continuous mRNA ribbon with one genuine paired-stem hairpin loop (rung tick-marks bridging two parallel self-paired sections, capped by a rounded open loop), a textbook-clear four-petal tRNA cloverleaf with a distinctly brighter anticodon petal and a separate plain amino-acid tail, and a knobbly two-lobed membrane-free ribosome. Used as the primary labelled figure; this was the 5th and final permitted attempt for this style)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; a false-colour macro surface view showing a single thin filament threading into a knobbly, irregular, membrane-free two-lobed mass (terracotta + blue, matching this atlas's ribosome house colours) with a small angular knotted/folded filament nearby reading as a compact folded tRNA. Confirmed on a magnified crop: zero baked text anywhere, cool-blue false-colour palette fills the frame edge-to-edge, no border. Not labelled, per project convention that the SEM plate is the surface/comparison image rather than a labelled diagram)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; baked-in text 'tm' appeared next to the tRNA's tail — a hard violation — and the tRNA rendered as an abstract ball-and-stick dumbbell/bone shape rather than a cloverleaf; the mRNA's attempted hairpin twisted into an ambiguous self-crossing figure-8 loop rather than a clean local stem-loop. Fix-prompt: apply the same four-petal-clover redescription that was being developed for textbook, ban circular bead markers, and describe the hairpin as a short, spatially bounded bobby-pin fold rather than an open-ended twist)
3d.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; no baked text and the tRNA cloverleaf now read beautifully, but the ribosome rendered with obvious MIRROR-SYMMETRY duplication — four lobes instead of two, a reflected kaleidoscope artifact — and the mRNA hairpin degenerated into stray disconnected vertical glitch lines. Two hard fails on this style — escalated toward gemini-3-pro-image per the model ladder, but the pro tier was returning HTTP 429 'quota exceeded' errors for the whole remainder of this session (shared API-key contention with a concurrent sibling DNA-render agent), confirmed transient/infrastructural by retrying after a wait and by successfully calling gemini-2.5-flash-image on other themes in the same window. Given the budget-discipline instruction not to loop on retries, continued iterating on gemini-2.5-flash-image instead of blocking indefinitely on the rate-limited pro tier)
3d.3: 429 quota error on gemini-3-pro-image (HTTP 429, 'You exceeded your current quota') on two separate attempts several seconds apart; not counted as a style attempt since no image was produced. Diagnosed as shared-key rate-limiting rather than a hard account spend-cap, since gemini-2.5-flash-image calls succeeded throughout the same window on other themes/microbes.
3d.4: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image, continuing on flash since pro stayed rate-limited; explicit anti-mirroring and single-strand-hairpin-bounding language fixed the ribosome duplication and the tRNA stayed a clean clover, but the mRNA's hairpin attempt came out as a small triangular fork/split rather than a closed loop — a cosmetic miss, not a double-helix risk, since the strand still reads as clearly single throughout. Fix-prompt: describe the loop tip explicitly as a rounded U-turn/hook, never a fork or V-split)
3d.5: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the hairpin now closes into a clear small ring the strand loops through and rejoins — unambiguously one strand folding on itself, confirmed on a magnified crop with no baked text anywhere. tRNA cloverleaf clean and distinct with a separate amino-acid tail; ribosome bilobed (large terracotta lobe roughly 55-60% vs a smaller blue lobe, a milder size contrast than requested but still visibly unequal, never mirrored/duplicated). Used as the final 3d render and for the labelled figure. Honest compromise: this style never got a working gemini-3-pro-image attempt due to persistent 429 rate-limiting outside this agent's control; the accepted flash-tier result meets every hard requirement (single strand, no baked text, no membrane, no mirrored duplicates) but the hairpin is a simpler closed loop without visible internal pairing rungs, and the ribosome's two lobes are less dramatically unequal than the textbook figure's)

watercolor.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed aged-paper background correct, but baked-in single-letter glyphs ('U', 'U', 'A', 'C') appeared beside the coloured base beads on the mRNA ribbon, and the tRNA rendered as a wooden dog-bone/wrench shape rather than a cloverleaf. Fix-prompt: replace circular beads with plain tick-dashes and redescribe the tRNA as a four-petal clover, matching the fix already being developed for textbook)
watercolor.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; no baked text this time and a lovely clean four-petal tRNA cloverleaf, but the mRNA hairpin instruction over-extended: the model painted two nearly-full-length parallel ribbons joined by only a small arch on one side, reading as two separate strands rather than one strand with a brief local self-paired stem. Fix-prompt: explicitly bound the hairpin to a short localized stretch — no more than one-eighth of the strand's total length — and describe it as a small bobby-pin bump, not a second ribbon)
watercolor.3: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the bounded-hairpin fix worked — the mRNA now reads clearly as ONE continuous painted ribbon for its full length with one small self-crossing knot/loop partway along, confirmed by tracing it visually end to end. Four-petal tRNA cloverleaf clean, distinct amino-acid tail, no baked text anywhere. Ribosome lobes read as similar in size rather than dramatically unequal (a minor, honestly-noted cosmetic softness on this secondary/context structure, not a hard violation of this plate's own do-not-draw list). Used as the final watercolor render and for the labelled figure)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons 'File:3d_tRNA.png', CC BY-SA 3.0 / GFDL 1.2+, Vossman — a PyMOL ribbon/stick rendering of PDB 1EHZ, yeast tRNA-Phe at 1.93 Angstrom resolution, the same molecule whose 1974 crystal structure first revealed the L-shaped tertiary fold. EXPLICITLY NOT a photograph — a computed structural model, stated plainly in the log, consistent with how this atlas's DNA and Ribosome sibling entries handle molecular-scale references. Viewed directly and confirmed to unmistakably show this plate's defining feature: the L-shaped fold, colour-coded by domain (orange CCA/acceptor tail, purple acceptor stem, red D-arm, blue anticodon arm with the anticodon in black, green T-arm), on a clean white background with no baked-in text, scale bar or watermark anywhere. Reads as ONE continuous folded strand throughout, never a DNA-style double helix. No edit_image.py step was needed since the source already carried no text/scale bar/border — only fetch_reference.py's own deterministic centre-crop-to-square + resize was applied (1061x1056 native, negligible ~5px trim, no content lost).
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; 2 flash-model fails (baked 'TN' text + bow-shaped tRNA; then a ladder-pattern risk + unclear tRNA-codon pairing) triggered escalation to gemini-3-pro-image, which nailed the cloverleaf shape immediately but baked literal base-letter glyphs onto every circular bead for 2 further attempts; switching every base marker from a circular bead to a plain tick-dash finally broke the letter-writing tendency and passed clean on the 5th and final permitted attempt
